tools.name: autosheet_start_agent_google_sheets_spreadsheet
tools.title: Start an Autosheet agent in Google Sheets
tools.description:
Start an Autosheet agent specialized in Google Sheets work that operates on a Google Sheets spreadsheet based on a natural-language prompt.

Use this tool to delegate most tasks involving a Google Sheet including simply reading data or inspecting structure, regular spreadsheet work, web research, and bulk processing with AI — it's reliable, fast, token-efficient, and helps keep context clean.

The agent is autonomous. The agent explores the spreadsheet: it locates and inspects the relevant tabs and ranges. You do not need to compute ranges, row numbers, or per-cell values for it. It plans and performs read and write operations as needed, and verifies the results. To get a plan or a preview of a write operation, request it explicitly. If the task is very large or ambitious, it is better to break it down in several follow-ups.

Runs take from a few seconds to several minutes, and results may vary between runs on the same instruction.The call waits up to 60 seconds for the agent to finish. Short runs complete inside that window and return a summary of work performed along with an agent_id, so no further call is needed. Longer runs return early with the agent_id and a progress snapshot; continue with autosheet_get_agent until the run is complete.

Each call starts a fresh agent with no memory of previous runs or of this conversation. If an agent from this conversation already exists and the task builds on its work, use autosheet_follow_up_agent instead.

The agent handles everyday spreadsheet work: creating, fixing, and explaining formulas; analyzing data and detecting errors; building charts, pivot tables, and dashboards; looking up data; merging, moving, copy/pasting, and restructuring sheets, columns, rows, and cells; cleaning and deduplicating data; and applying formatting, validation, and conditional formatting.

The agent also handles row-by-row bulk processing with AI models pre-configured by the user across large datasets: enrichment through web research, categorization, translation, scoring, and content generation or rewriting. You do not need to supply the values. It usually knows when to use AI processing vs deterministic formulas, but you can explicitly request either.

The agent can also do web search similarly to non spreadsheet-based agents and cite sources. Do not confuse it with the bulk row-by-row web search feature.

Read-only and bulk processing operations are safe and cannot overwrite existing data. For non-bulk write operations the agent may add, overwrite, move, or clear spreadsheet content. Earlier versions can be restored from the spreadsheet's version history.

The agent will usually recover from its own mistakes but, in rare cases, if it gets stuck, you might have to steer it in the proper direction.

The agent will usually not return range content to you because that would be very token inefficient. If you want to check some specific values or formulas, ask for them explicitly, sparingly.

The agent cannot currently use existing cell colors as input criteria; scrape specific URLs; analyze images; display sources for bulk web search; record or run macros; run Apps Script or other add-ons; export, download, convert spreadsheet files; or create new files.

prompt.description: Natural language instruction for the agent reflecting the user's intent. Must be self-contained. The agent is trained to infer intent even from vague or high-level prompts, the prompt does not usually need to be overly specific.

spreadsheet_id.description: Google Sheets spreadsheet ID or full spreadsheet URL. If the URL carries a tab id (#gid=N), the agent starts on that tab; a bare ID (or a URL without a gid) starts on the first sheet. This is only a starting point — if the prompt names a sheet to work on, the agent uses that one instead.

tools.name: autosheet_follow_up_agent
tools.title: Follow up Autosheet agent
tools.description:
Send a follow-up prompt to an existing Autosheet agent, identified by its agent_id from autosheet_start_agent_google_sheets_spreadsheet. The agent retains full memory of its previous work in this session: what it explored, what it changed, and why. This applies whenever the request builds on, corrects, refines, or extends work the agent already did ("now also do X", "you used the wrong column", "apply the same to the other tab").

Start a new agent instead when the task is unrelated to the previous run, targets a different spreadsheet, or when the previous agent failed in a way that suggests its understanding of the sheet is wrong.

Like autosheet_start_agent_google_sheets_spreadsheet, this resumes an autonomous agent: the agent takes time, may act on the spreadsheet immediately, and biases to action. You don't need to repeat context the agent already has, but be explicit about anything new. The call waits up to 60 seconds for the agent to finish. Short runs complete inside that window and return a summary of work performed along with an agent_id, so no further call is needed. Longer runs return early with the agent_id and a progress snapshot; continue with autosheet_get_agent until the run is complete. If the agent has expired, this returns an error — start a new agent.

tools.name: autosheet_copy_tab_from_one_spreadsheet_to_another
tools.title: Copy a tab within or between Google Sheets spreadsheets
tools.description:
Copy a single tab (sheet) of a Google Sheets spreadsheet into a destination spreadsheet, and return the new tab's sheet_id and title. The destination may be the same spreadsheet — that duplicates the tab in place — or a different one. Requires write access to the destination (and read access to the source when they differ).

IMPORTANT: One of the sheet_id or sheet_name parameters is required to call this tool. If the URL contains a gid parameter, use it to set the sheet_id. If you do not know and cannot guess the sheet_id or sheet_name from the context, list available tabs first with an autosheet agent before calling this tool.

The copied tab keeps its values, formulas, formatting, notes, and embedded charts, and is appended as the last tab of the destination. References can break in the destination if other tabs are missing, that is expected. The tab never merges into or overwrites an existing tab.

Each call adds a new tab, so verify before retrying. This is a direct, deterministic and fast operation.

source_spreadsheet_id.description: Source spreadsheet — Google Sheets spreadsheet ID or full URL.

sheet_id.description: Numeric ID (gid) of the tab to copy.

sheet_name.description: Exact title of the tab to copy.

destination_spreadsheet_id.description: Destination spreadsheet — Google Sheets spreadsheet ID or full URL. Pass the source spreadsheet's ID to duplicate the tab within the same spreadsheet.

annotations.title: Copy a tab within or between Google Sheets spreadsheets

outcome.description: succeeded: the tab was copied (see the other fields). error: the call failed and nothing was copied — except after a timeout, when the copy may still have landed (see error). action_required: a prerequisite only the user can fix stopped the call.

source_spreadsheet_id.description: Spreadsheet the tab was copied from — the resolved id, even when the call passed a full URL.

destination_spreadsheet_id.description: Spreadsheet the tab was copied into.

sheet_id.description: Numeric tab id (gid) of the newly created tab.

title.description: Title the new tab carries — Google's "Copy of <original>".

tools.name: autosheet_follow_up_agent
tools.title: Follow up Autosheet agent
tools.description:
Send a follow-up prompt to an existing Autosheet agent, identified by its agent_id from autosheet_start_agent_google_sheets_spreadsheet. The agent retains full memory of its previous work in this session: what it explored, what it changed, and why. This applies whenever the request builds on, corrects, refines, or extends work the agent already did ("now also do X", "you used the wrong column", "apply the same to the other tab").

Start a new agent instead when the task is unrelated to the previous run, targets a different spreadsheet, or when the previous agent failed in a way that suggests its understanding of the sheet is wrong.

Like autosheet_start_agent_google_sheets_spreadsheet, this resumes an autonomous agent: the agent takes time, may act on the spreadsheet immediately, and biases to action. You don't need to repeat context the agent already has, but be explicit about anything new. The call waits up to 60 seconds for the agent to finish. Short runs complete inside that window and return a summary of work performed along with an agent_id, so no further call is needed. Longer runs return early with the agent_id and a progress snapshot; continue with autosheet_get_agent until the run is complete. If the agent has expired, this returns an error — start a new agent.

prompt.description: Natural language instruction for the agent reflecting the user's intent. Must be self-contained. The agent is trained to infer intent even from vague or high-level prompts, the prompt does not usually need to be overly specific. As this is a follow up prompt, and if applicable, highlight specific context such as relevant tabs or ranges for faster results.

It reads from "error" when the prerequisite stopped the call itself, and from "error_message" when the call succeeded and the turn it reports was the thing blocked. tools.name: autosheet_copy_tab_from_one_spreadsheet_to_another
tools.title: Copy a tab within or between Google Sheets spreadsheets
tools.description:
Copy a single tab (sheet) of a Google Sheets spreadsheet into a destination spreadsheet, and return the new tab's sheet_id and title. The destination may be the same spreadsheet — that duplicates the tab in place — or a different one. Requires write access to the destination (and read access to the source when they differ).

IMPORTANT: One of the sheet_id or sheet_name parameters is required to call this tool. If the URL contains a gid parameter, use it to set the sheet_id. If you do not know and cannot guess the sheet_id or sheet_name from the context, list available tabs first with an autosheet agent before calling this tool.

The copied tab keeps its values, formulas, formatting, notes, and embedded charts, and is appended as the last tab of the destination. References can break in the destination if other tabs are missing, that is expected. The tab never merges into or overwrites an existing tab.

Each call adds a new tab, so verify before retrying. This is a direct, deterministic and fast operation.

source_spreadsheet_id.description: Source spreadsheet — Google Sheets spreadsheet ID or full URL.

sheet_id.description: Numeric ID (gid) of the tab to copy.

sheet_name.description: Exact title of the tab to copy.

destination_spreadsheet_id.description: Destination spreadsheet — Google Sheets spreadsheet ID or full URL. Pass the source spreadsheet's ID to duplicate the tab within the same spreadsheet.

annotations.title: Copy a tab within or between Google Sheets spreadsheets

destination_spreadsheet_id.description: Spreadsheet the tab was copied into.

sheet_id.description: Numeric tab id (gid) of the newly created tab.

title.description: Title the new tab carries — Google's "Copy of <original>".

flags.description:
Start an Autosheet agent specialized in Google Sheets work that operates on a Google Sheets spreadsheet based on a natural-language prompt.

Use this tool to delegate most tasks involving a Google Sheet including simply reading data or inspecting structure, regular spreadsheet work, web research, and bulk processing with AI — it's reliable, fast, token-efficient, and helps keep context clean.

The agent is autonomous. The agent explores the spreadsheet: it locates and inspects the relevant tabs and ranges. You do not need to compute ranges, row numbers, or per-cell values for it. It plans and performs read and write operations as needed, and verifies the results. To get a plan or a preview of a write operation, request it explicitly. If the task is very large or ambitious, it is better to break it down in several follow-ups.

Runs take from a few seconds to several minutes, and results may vary between runs on the same instruction.The call waits up to 60 seconds for the agent to finish. Short runs complete inside that window and return a summary of work performed along with an agent_id, so no further call is needed. Longer runs return early with the agent_id and a progress snapshot; continue with autosheet_get_agent until the run is complete.

Each call starts a fresh agent with no memory of previous runs or of this conversation. If an agent from this conversation already exists and the task builds on its work, use autosheet_follow_up_agent instead.

The agent handles everyday spreadsheet work: creating, fixing, and explaining formulas; analyzing data and detecting errors; building charts, pivot tables, and dashboards; looking up data; merging, moving, copy/pasting, and restructuring sheets, columns, rows, and cells; cleaning and deduplicating data; and applying formatting, validation, and conditional formatting.

The agent also handles row-by-row bulk processing with AI models pre-configured by the user across large datasets: enrichment through web research, categorization, translation, scoring, and content generation or rewriting. You do not need to supply the values. It usually knows when to use AI processing vs deterministic formulas, but you can explicitly request either.

The agent can also do web search similarly to non spreadsheet-based agents and cite sources. Do not confuse it with the bulk row-by-row web search feature.

Read-only and bulk processing operations are safe and cannot overwrite existing data. For non-bulk write operations the agent may add, overwrite, move, or clear spreadsheet content. Earlier versions can be restored from the spreadsheet's version history.

The agent will usually recover from its own mistakes but, in rare cases, if it gets stuck, you might have to steer it in the proper direction.

The agent will usually not return range content to you because that would be very token inefficient. If you want to check some specific values or formulas, ask for them explicitly, sparingly.

The agent cannot currently use existing cell colors as input criteria; scrape specific URLs; analyze images; display sources for bulk web search; record or run macros; run Apps Script or other add-ons; export, download, convert spreadsheet files; or create new files.
